text:
rachel: Quick follow-up from the RFC review: propose a delta-first bundle layout that makes partial apply and resume robust for air-gapped installs. Want to capture tradeoffs before I draft the follow-up RFC.
tom: Sounds good. What do you mean by delta-first?
rachel: Two ideas: 1) bundle contains a sequence of ordered deltas + strong tombstone metadata; 2) each delta has a safepoint and resume token so we can recover mid-apply without full rollback.
priya: Important: resume tokens must be content-addressed and include the hash of the operator-ack metadata so we can prove what was applied after a disconnect.
lee: Safety concern: if we allow resume we must avoid partial activation that leaves services in mixed state. Suggest defining an activation boundary: services switch over only at safepoints.
tom: Draft flow I picture: download bundle -> verify basic checksums -> apply deltas in order -> at each safepoint run health probes -> if probes pass, persist resume token and continue -> if probes fail, stop and expose rollback plan.
rachel: Exactly. Also want a small dry-apply mode for operators to run locally (no activation) that emits a list of file/manifest changes + predicted service impact.
priya: For air-gapped installs we can’t rely on remote signatures. Strategy: include an operator-signed approval block OR a sealed-verifier artifact that can be validated later when connectivity resumes.
lee: UX note: require explicit operator confirm when using sealed-verifier-without-signature. That should add a small recorded justification field in activation metadata.
infra-bot: artifact-validator v3.2 reported: previous resume token mismatch on node-43 during last test. See logs: https://ci.redwood/v/9001 :warning:
priya: Edge case: what if the resumed delta expects new runtime config keys that weren’t present at initial unpack? We should add a preflight shim that validates runtime compatibility before applying a delta.
tom: Proposed manifest fields to include in RFC: delta_id, parent_delta_ids, safepoint_marker, tombstone_list, resume_token_hash, preflight_checks (list), estimated-downtime-ms.
rachel: Also propose a compact tombstone index so we can GC removed blobs across many deltas without scanning the entire history. Garbage collection should be operator-initiated and require a compact-snapshot activation to avoid accidental deletes.
lee: Operational hooks: expose `redwood-resume --activation <id> --from <resume-token>` and `redwood-dryapply --bundle <file>` with human prompts. Also require a `--force` flag documented as destructive.
priya: Monitoring: emit events: resume_attempt, resume_success, resume_failure, tombstone_gc_requested. Include bundle-id in events.
tom: Performance thought: delta-first is great for bandwidth-limited installs but increases verifier complexity. Maybe ship a small reference verifier library in the on-prem agent to avoid version skew.
rachel: Agree; include verifier lib compatibility matrix in RFC. Also we should add a migration path for older bundles: importer that converts legacy full-image bundles into delta-first sequences (best-effort).
lee: Can we add a quick example in the RFC of a resume token structure? e.g.:
```
resume_token: "sha256:abcd1234..|apply-index:7|operator:priya|tz:2026-03-22T11:12:00Z"
```
priya: That format is fine if we insist on canonical ordering and UTF-8 normalization before hashing. Document it.
infra-bot: nightly-sanity job #1289: delta-apply tests passed on ubuntu-22.04 but failed on rhel8 conductor with tombstone GC test :x:
tom: OK next steps: rachel drafts RFC with example manifest, resume API, GC playbook, and dry-apply UX. Priya will enumerate verifier edge cases. Lee will write the operator confirmation language.
rachel: Thanks. I'll circulate a draft by EOD and set up a short sync next Tue. cc @eng-sre @release-ops for visibility.
